mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay depressed while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, discretionary trips shift away from shopping districts and keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks. The mechanism is a commuter-demand shortfall rather than a one-week noise effect.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean for the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES remains at or below -20 and TRANSIT remains at or below -25 for most weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS above baseline marks broader mobility normalization and spills into nearby leisure and shopping trips, lifting RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks. The effect requires PARKS to stay positive, not just spike once.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses above 0 and remains positive for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the prior 4-week mean within 14 days after PARKS stays above 0 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while GROCERY_PHARM is near baseline, routine neighborhood replacement trips substitute for discretionary retail trips and push RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks. This is a home-centered substitution mechanism, not a supply shock.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL stays above +8 and GROCERY_PHARM stays between -5 and 0 for most weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT drops further from an already weak level, fewer cross-town shopping trips occur and RETAIL_REC falls with about a one-week lag. The mechanism activates only after a meaningful transit contraction, not during flat transit conditions.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -30 after being above -30 in the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7 days of TRANSIT crossing from above -30 to below -30.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS together with improving GROCERY_PHARM indicates warmer-weather out-of-home activity and more combined errand chains, which should lift RETAIL_REC over a four-week horizon. The effect is strongest when both series improve at the same time.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays below its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days despite PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both trending upward for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A short-run drop in WORKPLACES below the recent range signals a renewed shift to home-based activity that immediately reduces impulse and lunch-time shopping, pushing RETAIL_REC down within two weeks. The effect should be visible only when WORKPLACES breaks its recent floor.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls 3 or more points below its previous weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after WORKPLACES falls at least 3 points below its prior weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both recover together, commuting density and downtown presence rise enough to support more retail visits, so RETAIL_REC increases over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if only one of the two series improves.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days while both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES increase from their current levels.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-spring regime, a positive PARKS reading combined with low GROCERY_PHARM implies more discretionary outdoor time and less pantry-stocking behavior, which should move RETAIL_REC upward within one week. This is a fast seasonal substitution mechanism.
candidate_trigger: PARKS is above 0 while GROCERY_PHARM is at or below -3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within 7 days when PARKS is positive and GROCERY_PHARM is at or below -3.
